memo.verdict: Neutral at 692.5p (18 September 2026). Progress, not park: the record stays live because the cleared branch (Canada launched on time and mid-single-digit core growth in FY2027) is dated inside six months and its odds are a little under even (0.42). Bullish below about 640p, the eighteen-month price at which the modal path clears the 20 percent bar (about 615p under the adverse drop-through; about 569p on three years), or on delivery of both the Canada launch and the core's FY2027 growth. Conviction: medium. The gate line does not park the case (management C, business quality C, predictability B, trackability B); the return does, at this price. The record flags that the business-quality C was rated with D live, and that on a reading of a 2 percent-margin, five-customer business as a D the gate would park the case on its own.
case: - The kind of case: an internal-change case in a business whose environment sets a low ceiling. Hilton Food is a contracted, cost-plus packer of meat for five leading grocers, earning a 2 percent margin and a 20 percent return on capital, whose profits fell for two years because of a seafood division it could not run and whose chief executive left abruptly in November 2025. A rebuilt leadership has cleaned up the portfolio, ring-fenced seafood and contracted two new geographies, and at 692.5p the shares already pay for the modest earnings recovery that produces.

- The change is internal, broad and dated. Eight of the twelve internal forces sit at B or better, three at A (chief executive B, other leaders A, strategy B, standards B, perimeter reduction A, new geographies A, new products B, balance sheet B), and the framework's screen rule is passed on both limbs (three forces strong; chief executive change plus a guidance increase). None of the screen's red flags applies in full: not a caretaker chief executive (bought 42,500 shares at 468p; took the permanent role 1 July 2026), not a presentation-only change (£79.8m banked), the guidance rise partly one-off (flagged), no crown-jewel sale (Foods Connected contracts retained), no empire-building, no dangerous leverage (1.4x), no debt-funded buyback. Price rises D: cost-plus, open-book, over 90 percent of raw-material cost passed through, raw meat about 80 percent of packed cost; no real or latent pricing power. Shareholder returns C: dividend flat in practice, cover rebuilding toward 2.0x, no buyback. Acquisitions C: none by design.

- The forces outside the company lean the other way (external forces D) and set the ceiling: supply side D (global beef production -2 percent 2027, -3 percent 2028; Australian cattle availability falling sharply from 2027; Irish throughput -16 percent; European retail beef prices over 50 percent higher; haddock up to 90 percent; Peruvian fishmeal up 90 percent; retailers resist real-time pass-through and processing costs are fixed annually); competition D (West core meat profit -20.5 percent on Ireland and mix; Lidl Ireland holding a 15 to 20 percent price gap; Tesco moved to 100 percent Scottish beef for Scottish stores and Hilton ceased supplying it; retailers integrating backwards, ABP and Kepak moving up); political and regulatory D (the FDA restriction on Foppen outlasting every date; Saudi Vision 2030 a tailwind not yet in the numbers; EU packaging and deforestation rules; UK National Insurance rises); own cycle B (troughed in FY2026 on seafood, turning: H1 beat, guidance raise, volume acceleration, cash turn); demand C (mass-market protein flat; structural only in Central European convenience, +26 percent; trading down within beef, steak margins 17 to 23 percent against mince 2 to 5 percent); macro C (two-thirds of revenue outside the UK; a 10 percent sterling appreciation cost £2.2m of FY2025 profit; the Australian dollar now a tailwind); disruption C (plant-based retreating; automation strengthening in Hilton's favour, about 10 percent labour reduction; fermentation a 2030s tail); catch-all C (Strait of Hormuz a risk to the Saudi step only). Change Forces B: internal A, external D; the external headwinds do not stop the programme, they limit its output to mid-single digits.
counter_case: - The risks research's "false friend", sharpened by the September print, at full force. The guidance upgrade is entirely technical (Dalco's £3.7m excluded, the Australian dollar), and beneath it constant-currency continuing profit fell 8.9 percent for the half. The £41.2m cash swing is a seasonal working-capital unwind of the kind the research warned would flatter free cash flow while profitability decays. Revenue growth of 15.3 percent is beef inflation over volumes of 0.6 percent in the West, the region that is two-thirds of the business. The anchor customer has just shown, inside a renewed partnership, that it can remove a volume stream at will. Canada has already slipped a year and £20m, will run at 10 to 15 percent higher cost than its competitors, and has Hilton bearing all build inflation against a customer whose pricing is protected. Foppen has outlasted every date. The auditor would not rely on the controls. The executives own almost nothing. And on this the market has re-rated the shares 42 percent in six months to a multiple with 18 to 29 percent of downside to the stock's own trough levels (570p at 9.4x; 491p at 8.1x; 447.69p at the last such episode). A sceptic who believed all of this would expect the FY2026 results on 7 April 2027 to show H2 profit below H2 FY25, the Canada launch to slip into mid-2027, and the shares to give back the rally to about 500p.

- At 'Foundations': everything the thesis leans on is in the customer's gift: contracted volumes that the customer shifts 5 to 7 percent of tactically and has just removed a stream of; a margin capped by open-book audit and benchmarking; raw material owned by suppliers whose costs are rising; retailers preferring captive-supply suppliers since the pandemic, which Hilton is not. On this reading the business is a 2 percent-margin utility to five customers, a D under 'Business', and the gate parks the case on its own.
triggers: - Price: bullish below about 640p (eighteen-month clearing price on the modal path; about 615p under the adverse drop-through; 569p on three years; 655p and 578p on the three-branch blend). Trough-multiple downside: 570p at 9.4x, 491p at 8.1x on 60.63p; 602p on the uncleared branch's 64p at 9.4x.

- Canada (Key Driver): Alarm if launch after Q1 2027; Invalidate if capex above £100m or launch after mid-2027. Watch Walmart trials, equipment testing late 2026, the January 2027 launch, the January 2027 update and the 7 April 2027 results.

- Core growth (Key Driver): Alarm if West core meat volumes negative in H2 FY26 or H1 FY27; Invalidate if group volumes below -1 percent for a year or the Oceania margin below 3.0 percent. Watch West core meat volumes, Polish volumes, East and West adjusted operating profit; modal case 4 to 6 percent core growth in FY2027 with West volumes flat to +1 percent.

- Seafood resolution (Key Driver): Alarm if no FDA decision by December 2026; Invalidate if no resolution or sale by mid-2027. Watch Foppen's regulatory status and losses, Seachill's H2 FY26 profit, any sale announcement and its price (a distressed disposal is a case risk).
- Customer sourcing shift (Key Risk): Alarm on any announced in-sourcing or re-tender by Tesco, Woolworths or Ahold; Invalidate on a core contract lost at renewal.

- Beef supply and mix (Key Risk): Alarm on a raw-material price spike above 15 percent; Invalidate on an Oceania margin below 3.0 percent. Watch UK and Irish cattle prices and throughput, Australian cattle availability, the steak-to-mince mix.
